task:
Create a production-quality early-medieval Norman-inspired Spearman in Blender from the reference image. This run owns only the Blender asset and export; do not modify Unity C# or scene/prefab files.

Reference-derived requirements:
- final standing height exactly 1.1 Blender meters from ground to helmet apex, realistic 7.5-head adult proportions
- padded quilted gambeson, knee-length blue team-color tabard, leather belt, gloves, wrapped boots, modest shoulder protection
- conical steel helmet with nasal guard, rim, visible rivets, chainmail aventail
- round shield with wooden planks, realistic thickness, metal rim and boss, blank/team emblem area
- primary weapon is a long ash-wood spear with metal socket and leaf-shaped spearhead
- no primitives-as-final-blockout, no toy proportions, no oversized head, no fantasy plate armor
- one standard Humanoid-compatible armature only: Root, Hips, spine/chest/neck/head, standard left/right shoulders/arms/hands and legs/feet/toes. No custom weapon bones.
- create SpearSocket parented to RightHand and ShieldSocket parented to LeftHand as non-deforming attachment empties/transforms, with separate spear and shield objects parented to those sockets
- LOD0 9,000-12,000 triangles; LOD1 3,000-5,000 triangles; shared rig/material atlas layout
- keep renderer/material groups low: Team cloth/emblem, Body/Leather/Wood, Metal
- complete non-overlapping UVs suitable for a single main 2K atlas
- author Actions at 30 fps: Idle 2.5s loop, Walk 1.0s loop, RunCharge 0.75s loop, Attack 0.95s, Block 1.2s loop, Hit 0.4s, Death 1.35s. Root motion disabled; attack pullback/thrust/recovery and death collapse must be readable.
- use solid-mode silhouette inspections and verify hand/socket contacts, shield grip, spear grip, feet-on-ground, helmet/head seating, boss/shield seating, spearhead/socket seating
- inspect front/back/left/right/top/bottom and three-quarter views before final review
- save editable source to D:\unity_projects\OpenEmpiresTemp\Spearman_Rebuild_Source.blend
- export FBX to D:\unity_projects\OpenEmpiresTemp\SM_Spearman_Rebuild.fbx using Unity-compatible -Z forward, Y up, applied scale, deform bones only where appropriate, and baked animations
- do not touch the existing current Spearman FBX or prefab
